explanations.explanation: Firstfruits it is, friend. Moses says, “…take some of the firstfruits of all your produce from the soil of the land…” That's the first of the harvest going in the basket. When a tray comes out of my oven, that first cookie gets ALL the attention, so I can picture how special first-of-the-batch is.

Surplus is the extra left once everything else is counted, and that's not the word Moses uses. He says the basket gets the firstfruits of all their produce. So the first of the harvest goes in, not the pile at the end. Good thinking, friend, but the word the text gives is firstfruits.

Gleanings are the bits picked up afterward, and that's not what Moses says here. He says to take some of the firstfruits of all their produce and put them in a basket. Firstfruits means the first of the harvest. It's the front of the line, friend, not the cleanup crew.

explanations.answer: I have entered the land the LORD swore to give us
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The worshiper says, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.” Notice who did the swearing: the LORD did. The worshiper is standing there with a basket as proof that the promise came through.

explanations.answer: I have gathered more than any year before this one
explanations.explanation: No bragging rights in this declaration, friend. The worshiper doesn't compare harvests or mention how big the crop was. What he says is that he has entered the land the LORD swore to our fathers to give us. It's a declaration about the LORD's promise, not about a record-breaking year.

explanations.answer: I have kept every vow my fathers made to the LORD
explanations.explanation: That one sounds nice, but it isn't what the worshiper says. He never mentions vows the fathers made. He says he has entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us. So the LORD is the one who made the promise, and the worshiper is saying it came true.

Easy to read it that way, but the worshiper says something different. The wandering Aramean went down to Egypt “…few in number…” He lived there, and that's where he “…became a great nation, mighty and numerous.” So the growing happened in Egypt, not before he got there.

Right, friend. The worshiper says the wandering Aramean went down to Egypt “…few in number…” It was after he lived there that he “…became a great nation, mighty and numerous.” Small family on the way in, great nation by the time the story gets going.

explanations.answer: He hears their voice and sees their affliction
explanations.explanation: That's it. The worshiper says, “…the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.” They called out, and He heard and saw. Two actions, friend, and both belong to the LORD. I think that's a comfort.

explanations.answer: He softens the hearts of the Egyptians
explanations.explanation: The worshiper never says anything about the Egyptians' hearts changing. What he says is that the LORD heard their voice and saw their affliction, toil, and oppression. The very next thing is that the LORD brought them out of Egypt. So the story goes toward rescue, not toward the Egyptians getting nicer.

explanations.answer: He gives them rest in the land of Goshen
explanations.explanation: Goshen never comes up in this declaration, friend. Here's what the worshiper says: “So we called out to the LORD, the God of our fathers; and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.” They called, and the LORD heard their voice and saw what they were going through. That's the answer. I think this part is heavy, and being heard and seen is the whole point of it.

explanations.answer: To this land flowing with milk and honey
explanations.explanation: That's right. The worshiper says, “And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” Notice the word “gave.” The land is a gift, and the basket in his hands is what the gift grew.

explanations.answer: Back to Haran beyond the Euphrates River
explanations.explanation: Haran, friend? That's a long walk backward, and the worshiper never takes it. He says the LORD brought them to “…this place…” and gave them “…this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” The LORD is taking them forward, into the gift. I've been moved around a lot in my life, from a bin to a counter to a drawer, but nobody ever sent me back to the bin. Forward is the direction here.

explanations.answer: To the wilderness at the foot of Sinai
explanations.explanation: Sinai never comes up in this declaration, friend. After the LORD brings them out of Egypt, the worshiper says, “And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” The place he names is the land the LORD gave, and that's where the basket comes from.

True, friend. Moses says, “Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.” So the basket is set before the LORD, and then the worshiper bows down. Basket down, then bow down. I like that order.

The text says the opposite, friend. Moses says, “Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.” The worshiper doesn't just drop the basket and head home. He bows down.

Rejoices is right. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” The word is rejoice, and the reason is the good things the LORD gave. I think that's a fine reason to smile, friend.

Foreigner is right, and look who got an invitation. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you…” That's a person just living among them, and the text hands them a seat at the celebration. I know a little about being the new one in the room, and a seat at the table is a beautiful thing, friend.

Mourning is the opposite of the mood here, friend. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” The basket is set down, the worshiper has bowed, and now it's time for joy. The text says rejoice.

A king never walks into this verse, friend. The ones who share the rejoicing are the worshiper, the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among them. That second blank wants the foreigner. It's an ordinary person who happens to be living among them.

Fasts? Friend, the basket just got set down and the worshiper has bowed. Nobody's skipping the party! Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” Rejoicing is the word for this moment, and I'd say a growling stomach is a poor fit for it.

True. In the third year, the year of the tithe, Moses says to give it to four groups: the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. The reason he gives is that they may eat and be filled within the gates. I count four names on that list, and the tithe is for every one of them.

The text says it's true, friend. Moses says that in the third year they are to give the tithe “…to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, that they may eat and be filled within your gates.” All four groups are named, one after another. Nobody gets skipped in that list.

The giver says the opposite, friend. He declares, “I have not eaten any of the sacred portion while in mourning…” So he's telling the LORD that he did not do that. Watch for the word “not,” because it matters a lot in a declaration like this.

Right. The giver declares, “I have not eaten any of the sacred portion while in mourning, or removed any of it while unclean, or offered any of it for the dead.” It's a list of things he says he did not do. He's not admitting to anything, and I'd say that's a pretty confident thing to say out loud.

explanations.answer: I have done everything You commanded me
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The giver says, “I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me.” Everything. That's a big word to say out loud in front of the LORD, and he says it.

explanations.answer: I have done most of what You asked of me
explanations.explanation: Most is a sneaky little word, and the giver doesn't use it. He says, “I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me.” Everything is a much bigger word than most. I once told myself I'd do most of the dishes, and nobody was proud of that.

explanations.answer: I have done all the Levites asked of me
explanations.explanation: The giver isn't answering to the Levites here, friend. He says to the LORD, “I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me.” The Levites are among the people who receive the tithe. The commands he's talking about came from the LORD.

Bless is right. The giver says, “Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel…” That's the request that follows all the giving. He turns from what he did to what he's asking the LORD to do.

Land is right. He asks the LORD to bless “…Your people Israel and the land You have given us as You swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.” So he's asking for blessing on the people and on the place they live. And once again, the land is called a gift.

This is a prayer for blessing, friend, not for judging. The giver says, “Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel…” The word is bless. After a declaration like this one, that's what he asks for.

No temple is mentioned in this prayer. The giver asks the LORD to bless “…Your people Israel and the land You have given us…” The second blank wants the land. It's the same land the LORD swore to their fathers.

Test isn't on the menu in this prayer. The giver asks the LORD to “…bless Your people Israel and the land You have given us…” That's a request for blessing, from someone who has just finished giving. So the first blank is bless.

explanations.answer: With all their heart and all their soul
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says, “You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.” That's all of it, not just a piece. I think that's a fair way to say it: halfway doesn't make a good batch of anything.

explanations.answer: On the feast days and in the good seasons
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't tie this to feast days or good seasons, friend. He says, “You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.” The command is about how they follow, with heart and soul. Seasons never come up.

explanations.answer: Whenever the priests come to remind them
explanations.explanation: No reminder is mentioned in this verse. Moses says, “You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.” That's the kind of following that doesn't wait for someone to knock on the door. It comes from the heart and the soul.

explanations.answer: They are His people and treasured possession
explanations.explanation: That's what Moses says. “And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised…” Treasured is a warm word, friend. It's the kind of thing you say about something you keep close.

explanations.answer: They are His workers and paid laborers
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't talk about paychecks in this verse. He says, “And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised…” A treasured possession is something much closer than a hired hand. No clock-in required.

explanations.answer: They are His people for one generation
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't put a time limit on it. He says, “And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised…” The words are His people and treasured possession. Nothing in the verse says it runs out after one generation.

True, friend. Moses says the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations He has made, in praise, name and honor. That's three things. The verse adds that Israel will be a holy people to the LORD, as He has promised.

The text says it's true, friend. Moses says the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations He has made, in praise, name and honor. All three are in the promise. The verse also says Israel will be a holy people to the LORD, as He has promised.
